# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL (about $32.90)**
- It has 4 independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and an adjustable current of 0.25A to 3A. Its LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance for each cell.
- It also has capacity-grading and storage modes, and fits cells from 10440 to 32650, including protected 21700s.
- Best Batteries rated it 4.3/5. 1Lumen and a separate reviewer both liked it.
- Caveats: it defaults to a high charge current, so lower it with the Curr button for small or older cells. One reviewer found it sometimes ended NiMH charges early or mistook NiMH for Li-ion, so watch the first minutes. It doesn't list LiFePO4 support.
- [Buy / see price (Best Batteries)](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/). Details: [1Lumen review](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/).

**Best if you want LiFePO4 support or fast charging: Nitecore UMS4 (about $38.95)**
- It has 4 independent slots, up to 3A in a single slot with a QC input, and 4A total. It supports Li-ion, LiFePO4 and NiMH.
- It also shows internal resistance, restores over-discharged Li-ion cells, and has reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection plus overtime protection.
- Without a QC source, output drops to 2A for a single slot.
- [Buy / see price (Best Batteries)](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/). Specs: [Nitecore](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4).

**Budget, simplest option: Tenergy TN270 ($18.99)**
- It's a 2-bay wall charger at 500 mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input, and its only listed protection is reverse-polarity detection.
- It suits a basic flashlight or headlamp setup.
- [Buy (Dealectric, affiliate)](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). Details: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-18650-battery-chargers-2026-xtar-vc4sl-nitecore-ums4-vapcell-s4-plus-review).

**Another option: Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics named it its Editor's Choice. It has selectable 500mA or 1000mA charging, an LCD, and wide chemistry support. That site earns affiliate commissions, and I couldn't get a direct product link, so check current reviews first.
- [Smashing Robotics roundup](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/)

## What to look for
Choose a charger with independent bays, so each cell is monitored separately, and with a stated termination method. Avoid no-name units that don't say how they decide a cell is full ([VoltRated guide](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)). Gentler, slower charging also helps cell life.

I couldn't verify the Vapcell S4 Plus from these results, so I left it out.

My pick is the XTAR VC4SL for most people, or the Nitecore UMS4 if you use LiFePO4 cells.
